_comment: One declarative source of truth for coding executors — LEAF-11-9 W1. tgw.coding_executor_catalog parses this; harness_session (executor chain + credential + binary discovery), harness_cli (binary path for the confined coder), and tgw.model_selector (known-executor set) all read it and hold NO hard-coded executor list. Adding an executor is an entry here plus one re-run of `tgw-coding-bootstrap --repair harness` — no code change. The built-in `stub` executor (offline canary, W0) has no entry: it needs no binary/credential/install. `enabled` is 'wired and installable on this host now'; a missing credential is a WARN (executor marked unavailable), never a failure. Edit /opt/TGW/tgw-lib/config/tgw-coding-executors.json to change it live; this repo copy is the committed default.

claude.note: Operator Claude subscription (flat-rate OAuth token) is the primary credential; the harness runs each session under a fresh HOME so it never touches an operator login dir.

codex.note: Also usable from a ChatGPT login copied to the per-session CODEX_HOME/auth.json (no env key needed).

deepseek.note: `dsh` (deepseek-harness) is operator-provisioned, not auto-installable yet — install_source null. Set enabled true once the binary is on this host.

gemini.note: Not installed on this host yet. This is the CLI-based @google/gemini-cli — a different product from Google Antigravity (GUI/IDE-extension + desktop app, no confirmed headless/CLI path as of 2026-09-12); Antigravity is explicitly not an executor here.

opencode.note: Multi-provider gateway. harness_session._run_opencode wired 2026-09-09; keeps all model-provider keys so opencode routes by model-id prefix (opencode/*, groq/*, openrouter/*:free, nous/*, anthropic/*). OpenCode Zen (pay-per-token) and OpenCode Go ($10/mo quota-priced subscription, verified 2026-09-12) are one account, not two separate credential systems: per opencode.ai's own docs, you sign in to Zen, subscribe to Go, and reuse 'your API key' -- same key, different local routing registration. CORRECTED 2026-09-13 (checked against opencode.ai/docs/go and /docs/providers directly, not assumed): OpenCode does NOT document any env var for its own Zen/Go tiers -- OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY/OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY in credential_env below are this repo's own placeholder names, not anything opencode itself reads. The only working path for either tier is the interactive `opencode auth login -p <tier>` (or TUI `/connect`) writing to ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json -- confirmed live on this host (`opencode auth list` shows both Zen and Go entries there). Setting either env var alone does nothing; this was empirically observed before this correction ('key setup alone didn't work, CLI auth did') and is now explained rather than just noted. Which tier serves a call is decided by the model id in config/model-availability.json (models_free / models_go / models_paid_via_zen). GROQ_API_KEY (live groq/* alternate) and NOUS_API_KEY ($20 funded balance -- no spend-metering hook exists yet, see cost_policy there) are real documented env vars for those (non-OpenCode-gateway) providers. Default coding model: opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free (free tier on the zen key; deepseek-v4-flash on that key is exhausted). The right model per role/risk is leaf 11.8's job. All key values remain operator-provisioned; none are stored here.

agy.note: Operator-provisioned agent CLI, not installed on this host yet.
